div.p: Clears the selection, then takes one snapshot: the columns on display and the number the first row is drawn with
The stages, in order: select enum filter sort slice select -e view
The filter and map bodies as moonblade
Spawns xan, buffers stdout, calls back
Reads the row id out of the first cell, cuts that cell from every line, and builds a csv.Row per line
nvim_buf_set_lines over the whole buffer, nomodifiable
Extmarks for the marked rows, the marked columns and the selection
Back to the column the user was in, since the new text has new widths
A decoration provider: nvim asks for each line as it draws it
nvim asks per line, and the layout says which row that line holds, so the row number is drawn in the gutter
